text:
maria: seeing a sharp tail-latency bump in rack-r3 this morning, looks correlated with a handful of preemptible slices getting hot. sample: 99p gen latency jumped from 120ms -> 900ms for small-slice tenants.

devin: saw that too. graph shows 3 nodes with bursted GPU utilisation + egress p99 spikes. might be noisy neighbor on a shared slice.

maria: markers: all affected jobs are small-slice (0.25 GPU), many are short-lived chat completions. burstiness causes KV cache churn across tenants.

kevin: can we throttle the small-slice burst rate or add token-bucket shaping per-tenant? current scheduler gives them instant slot credit.

anika: to add: when many short requests keep creating new KV contexts, prefix cache miss rate goes up and we see spike in memory pressure -> eviction storms. same pattern as last month but concentrated on rack.

devin: quick probe commands I ran: 
```
# top CPU/GPU
kubectl top pods --namespace=dedicated-r3 | sort -k3 -nr | head
# check egress
iftop -i eth0 -P | grep node-r3-
```
outputs show node-r3-21/22/23 with 3-4x egress compared to neighbors.

ops-bot: alert: rack-r3 node-r3-22 has consecutive preempt logs (preempted 7 containers in last 10m).

maria: hypothesis: scheduler soft-affinity allowed hot tenants to spread across multiple nodes in the same rack, causing cross-node KV invalidation and network amplification. Should we tighten soft-affinity for small-slice workloads to prefer single-node packing?

kevin: packing helps reduce cross-node KV churn but increases blast radius for noisy neighbor. tradeoff. another approach: enforce per-tenant burst cap (requests/sec) with a short refill window. lower latency-sensitive tenants can burst, but we throttle chatty ephemeral flows.

anika: also consider a small warmup policy: maintain a tiny reserved KV footprint for recurring tenants (LRU pin for 1-2 min) so repeated short bursts don't thrash. cost: small memory overhead but might fix p99.

devin: can we run a canary: for rack-r3, set scheduling policy to prefer packing for small-slice tenants and enable a 20req/s burst cap for 10s windows for a subset of tenants? measure 1h.

maria: +1. roll canary to 10% of affected tenant IDs first. add metrics: kv-cache miss rate, egress p95/p99, preempt events, and slice eviction counts.

kevin: note: need to coordinate with billing. burst caps will reduce egress spikes, likely cut extra charge from network. ops-finance should be aware. tagging: cost-impact: potential reduction in egress-burst billing.

anika: quick config snippet for scheduler patch (pseudo):
```
policy.small_slice:
  affinity: PACK_TIGHT
  burst_limit: 20reqs_per_sec
  burst_window: 10s
  kv_warmup: 90s_soft_pin
```

maria: I'll open a short-lived feature flag and deploy to the 10% cohort. Devin, can you add dashboards and alerts? Kevin, loop in finance for cost estimate.

devin: on it. creating dashboard tiles: rack-r3 kv miss %, per-tenant req/s distribution, egress p99. will add alert if kv miss > 15% AND p99 > 500ms for >5min.

kevin: pinging @finance on slack. also suggest a quick postmortem template in case canary worsens things.

maria: thanks. timeline: deploy canary in 20m, monitor for 60m, decide rollback/scale. if we see p99 drop >= 40% and kv miss drop >= 30% -> expand.

ops-bot: scheduled: canary policy rollout at 3102468240 by maria. auto-rollback on alert condition.

anika: small nit: ensure the policy won't force dedicated-pool tenants into shared racks. keep dedicated pool isolation intact.

maria: yep explicit exclusion for dedicated pool tags.

devin: will post results in ~90m. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
